Double jeopardy doesn't apply in this mistrial?

A mistrial is not a conviction... double Jeopardy means you cannot be tried and convicted of the same crime twice. If there has been no conviction for you to claim double Jeopardy on, then it's not double jeopardy.

This is not quite accurate. Double Jeopardy means you can't be tried (put in jeopardy) twice for the same crime independent of the outcome (unless mistrial). You can be acquitted of a crime, convicted, or have a mistrial with special circumstances and you are not allowed to be tried or punished again (without new facts, which usually means new charges/crimes). Most mistrials are not subject to double jeopardy.

This case ended in mistrial due to a hung jury, so double jeopardy does not apply unless the judge intervened.
